fixture: Real TypeScript SCIP references, imported HTTP handler alias, two call branches, reference-only callback, public/private members and linked test

factors.reason: Reachable symbols outside the directly selected declarations; saturates at 40.
Public exports, routes or public methods are exposed in the scope; actual compatibility changes require review.
Schema artifact exposure is a risk signal; schema migration semantics are not inferred.
Type/interface contract exposure; a breaking contract change is not established.
Authorization/security impact requires explicit change context; names alone are insufficient.
Concurrency consequences are not inferred from async syntax or static calls.
Only recorded effect edges establish observed effect exposure; other external effects remain unknown.
Recorded reads/writes indicate storage/resource exposure, not transaction correctness.
Line-weighted coverage of affected code files, only with matching snapshot hashes and verified reported lines. This does not prove whole-build freshness or test assertions.
Distinct owning modules; saturates at four.

score.interpretation: Versioned prioritization heuristic, not a defect probability or calibrated effort estimate. Unknown factors contribute no observed points and retain their weight in the upper bound.

impact.coverage: Synthetic LCOV with MD5 source-line checksums; reported execution counts are prescribed, tests not executed.

limits: Static shortest call paths, not runtime/data-flow proof; longer alternative paths are not enumerated.
No arbitrary external side-effect classification; persistence and unrecorded effects stay unknown unless supplied as change facts or recorded by an analyzer.
Workflow is a provisional recommendation; no collaborating agents, target tests or target source code were executed.
No real LLM answer quality, provider usage or end-to-end token savings measured.
